messages:
nina: Quick follow-up on the Service-Bound API Key idea from the RFC — thinking about a staged rollout + migration path. TL;DR: allow API keys to be bound to a service+project+route set and optionally exchangeable for short-lived service tokens. Thoughts on enforcement surface (edge vs app) and a low-risk migration?
ryan: I like the guardrail idea. Main tradeoff is runtime complexity if edge enforces route-level checks (more latency + policy sync).
alicia: Route-level at edge means centralized policy store + sync. If we do it, we should aim for eventual consistency and a dual-accept mode first (old keys still valid for X weeks).
samir: Question: why not do scoped keys + token-exchange at SDK level (client obtains ephemeral token from auth service) to avoid pushing policy to every edge?
nina: Good Q. Token-exchange reduces policy checks at call-time (auth service does it), but requires more network hops and complicates async/background jobs that only have static keys.
ryan: Also ops: token-exchange means we need a reliable token-gateway with high availability and metrics. If gateway fails, we'd need fallbacks.
alicia: Migration path idea: 1) Add metadata to keys (optional new fields: bound_service, allowed_routes[], ttl_scope) but keep current behavior. 2) Support "scope-aware" acceptance in auth library (returns a header showing scope). 3) Deploy edge validators that can read the scope header but be in "observe" mode for 2-4 weeks. 4) Enable enforce mode for canary customers.
samir: For background workers that can't do token exchange, we could allow a special service principal binding (long-lived but pinned to a compute identity) rather than binding to routes. Document the exception flow.
ryan: RBAC mapping: do we map these bound keys to existing roles or introduce a new "key-scope" layer? I prefer mapping to roles + an allowlist of routes to keep policy simple.
nina: Agreed. Keep roles for coarse-grain permissions and use key-scope for fine-grain routing restrictions. That avoids exploding role combinations.
alicia: Telemetry: we need to track: 401s from scope violations, token-exchange latency, auth-gateway QPS, number of keys migrated. Add per-key reason codes for failures so we can audit.
deploy-bot: deploy:auth-gateway v2 queued for canary on infra-prod at 2025-03-12T17:00Z.
samir: Security considerations: attacker with a leaked scoped key could still hit allowed routes. We should support forced revocation + replay detection (short token nonce) for exchanged tokens.
ryan: Implementation notes: DB schema change: add scope JSONB column to api_keys table (nullable). Add index on (bound_service) and a multi-tenant visibility check. We can backfill slowly.
alicia: Backfill plan: mark keys with inferred scopes from usage logs for opt-in beta users. Send owners an email prompt to opt-in.
nina: Rollout metrics + SLOs: auth-gateway target p99 add ~1-2ms. If we see >5% error surge during observe, rollback enforcement.
samir: SDK changes: expose `exchangeForServiceToken()` and a `dualAccept` flag that handles both legacy and scoped keys. Provide server-side middleware for background jobs to call token-gateway.
ryan: Docs + migration: create a migration guide, a small CLI to annotate keys, and an internal compatibility test suite. Start with infra and internal platform teams as first adopters.
alicia: Action items: 1) Nina draft a one-pager with the rollout timeline and failovers (due EOD Fri). 2) Ryan prototype edge validator (POC by next Wed). 3) Samir spec token-exchange API + replay protection (PR by next Tue). 4) I'll own telemetry dashboards + alerts.
nina: Perfect. Also add a small experiment: enable route-level observe for a single low-traffic route for 48h to validate false positives.
ryan: +1. If anyone wants to join the POC pairing session tomorrow 10am, ping me.
alicia: pinged the infra team leads to get the canary list.
nina: Thanks all — I'll post the one-pager when done. :thumbsup:
